details:
ASTRA – Astronaut Health & Wellness Monitoring System

ASTRA is a web-based astronaut health and wellness monitoring system designed to support continuous health observation during space missions. It provides a centralized platform where astronauts and mission teams can monitor vital signs, track health history, identify unusual changes, and receive alerts when readings exceed configured thresholds.

The system allows astronauts to record health measurements and wellness check-ins, while Mission Control can view astronaut health information through a dedicated dashboard. ASTRA uses rule-based alerts and personalized baseline analysis to identify unusual variations in health readings. It also includes notifications, historical data visualization, and access to NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) study information for research purposes.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

ASTRA aims to improve awareness of astronaut health conditions, support early identification of unusual health changes, and make health information easier for mission teams to monitor. By combining physical health tracking with wellness check-ins, it recognizes the importance of both physical and mental well-being during long-duration space missions. It can support better-informed decisions and contribute to astronaut safety and mission readiness.

Technology Used:

  • Frontend: React.js, Vite, JavaScript, HTML and CSS
  • Backend: Node.js and Express.js
  • Database: MySQL
  • Security: JWT authentication, bcrypt password hashing, and role-based access
  • Additional tools: NASA OSDR public data API, Axios, and VS Code
  • Platform: Web-based application accessible through a browser

Creativity and Innovation:

ASTRA combines vital-sign monitoring, personalized baseline anomaly detection, wellness tracking, and centralized Mission Control visualization in one platform. Instead of relying only on fixed health thresholds, it also compares recent readings against an individual's previous measurements to identify unusual variations. This combination provides a more personalized approach to astronaut health monitoring.

Factors Considered:

The project considers the challenges of long-duration space missions, the need for timely health information, individual differences in health baselines, data privacy, secure access, usability, and the importance of monitoring both physical and psychological wellness. ASTRA is designed as a research and demonstration platform that can be further developed and validated for real mission environments.
